items.en: Wisdom-Conduct, and the Bodhisattva's Own Unshared Dhyānas
items.zh: 無漏禪次第 · 慧行次第
parent: IV. Distinguishing the Sequence in Which Dhyāna-Pāramitā Is Explained

zh: 二、明無漏慧行次第之相。因聞四諦，即修三十七品，次入三解脫門，次用十六行觀分別四諦，次具十智、三無漏根，成就九修，獲九斷。如此略辨聲聞所行無漏慧行，次應說十二因緣觀門，即是辟支迦羅之所行無漏慧行。若菩薩次第成就，二乘學、無學所得智斷，是名從假入空，通觀具足也，故《大品經》云：「菩薩摩訶薩行般若波羅蜜，以方便力故，從乾慧地、入性地、八人地、見地、離欲地、阿羅漢、辟支佛地，皆行皆入而不取證。」
en: Second, clarifying the mark of the sequence of uncontaminated wisdom-conduct. Upon hearing the Four Noble Truths, one cultivates the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment; next enters the three gates of liberation; next uses the sixteen aspects of contemplation to distinguish the Four Noble Truths; next becomes complete in the ten kinds of knowledge and the three uncontaminated faculties, accomplishing the nine kinds of cultivation and attaining the nine severances. This is, in brief, the uncontaminated wisdom-conduct practiced by the śrāvaka. Next should be explained the gate of contemplating the twelve links of dependent origination, which is the uncontaminated wisdom-conduct practiced by the pratyekabuddha.

As for the bodhisattva accomplishing, in sequence, the knowledge and severance attained by both the trainees and the adepts of the two lesser vehicles — this is called "entering emptiness by way of the provisional," complete with thorough contemplation. Hence the Larger Sūtra says: "The bodhisattva-mahāsattva, practicing the perfection of wisdom, by the power of skillful means, passes from the ground of dry wisdom, into the ground of conforming nature, the ground of the eighth-stage practitioner, the ground of vision, the ground free of desire, the ground of the arhat, and the ground of the pratyekabuddha — practicing and entering every one of them, yet without taking hold of their realization."

zh: 次明菩薩不共禪次第者：一、自性禪；二、一切義禪；三、難禪；四、一切門禪；五、善人禪；六、一切行禪；七、除惱禪；八、此世他世樂禪；九、清淨淨禪。菩薩依是禪故，得大菩提果，具足十力、四無所畏、十八不共等一切佛法。此則略明菩薩從初發心修禪，次第行，次第學，次第道，乃至佛地，名住大涅槃深禪定窟。此義至釋第七、修證，第八、顯示果報中方乃具辨。
en: Next, clarifying the sequence of dhyāna unshared with the two lesser vehicles, proper to the bodhisattva alone: first, the dhyāna of self-nature; second, the dhyāna of every meaning; third, the difficult dhyāna; fourth, the dhyāna of every gate; fifth, the dhyāna of the good person; sixth, the dhyāna of every practice; seventh, the dhyāna that removes affliction; eighth, the dhyāna of joy in this life and lives to come; ninth, the pure-and-undefiled dhyāna. In dependence on these dhyānas, the bodhisattva attains the fruit of great bodhi, complete with the ten powers, the four kinds of fearlessness, the eighteen unshared qualities, and the whole of the buddhadharma.

This, then, briefly clarifies how the bodhisattva, from the very first arising of the mind, cultivates dhyāna, practicing in sequence, studying in sequence, walking the path in sequence, all the way to the ground of buddhahood — called abiding within the deep cave of dhyāna-concentration that is great nirvāṇa. This point will be treated in full only further below, where the seventh topic explains cultivation and realization, and the eighth reveals the fruits and rewards.

The nine unshared dhyānas named here (自性禪 and the rest) are the "nine kinds of great dhyāna" already referred to back in topic 2's discussion of why dhyāna alone is called pāramitā — this is their first full listing. Their names alone give a sense of what sets them apart from everything discussed so far: a "dhyāna of every meaning," a "dhyāna of every gate," a "dhyāna that removes affliction," a dhyāna of "joy in this life and lives to come" — attainments defined by comprehensive scope and benefit to others, not merely by depth of absorption. None of the nine is explained individually here, and the surviving ten fascicles never reach them: the cultivation and realization of dhyāna that is neither worldly nor world-transcending, where they would belong, is among the parts of the treatise left unwritten.

items.en: Must a Beginner Follow This Sequence?
parent: IV. Distinguishing the Sequence in Which Dhyāna-Pāramitā Is Explained

zh: 問曰：菩薩大士為通達諸禪淺深，具足一切佛法次第行，次第學，可如上說。今行人初學禪時，為當一向如上依次第修，為當不爾？答曰：今且欲明諸禪淺深相，一往作此次第分別，若論初心學人，隨所欲樂，便宜對治。易入泥洹者，從諸禪方便初門而修，不必定如前一一依次第。此義至內方便安心禪門中當廣分別。
en: Question: That a great bodhisattva, in order to penetrate the shallow and deep among the various dhyānas and become complete in the whole buddhadharma, practices in sequence and studies in sequence — this may indeed be said as above. But when a practitioner is first learning dhyāna, should they always cultivate strictly according to this sequence, or is this not necessarily so? Answer: What has just been said is meant only to clarify the shallow-to-deep pattern among the various dhyānas in a general way, this sequence given only in broad outline. As for a beginning student, they should follow whatever they find most inclined toward and easiest to apply as an antidote. One for whom entering nirvāṇa comes easily may cultivate starting from whichever preliminary gate among the various dhyānas' expedient means suits them, without necessarily having to follow the sequence given above step by step. This point will be treated fully further below, within the inner expedient means, in the gate of dhyāna for settling the mind.

A practical relief after all the taxonomy: the elaborate sequence just given is a map of the terrain, not a rigid itinerary every beginner must follow step by step. What a practitioner actually starts with should be matched to their own temperament and to whatever obstacle needs treating first — a theme this treatise will return to when it reaches the preliminary expedient means in later fascicles.

items.en: Four Ways Sequence and Non-Sequence Combine
parent: IV. Distinguishing the Sequence in Which Dhyāna-Pāramitā Is Explained

zh: 第二、簡非次第義。問曰：菩薩修禪為一向次第，修禪亦有非次第？答曰：此得為四：一、明次第；二、明非次第；三、明次第非次第；四、明非次第次第。今明次第，如上說。《大品經》云：「菩薩次第行，次第學，次第道。」非次第者，菩薩修法華、一行等諸三昧，觀平等法界非深非淺，故名非次第。如《無量義經》說：「行大直道，無留難故。」
en: Second, distinguishing what is not sequential. Question: Is the bodhisattva's cultivation of dhyāna always sequential, or is there also a cultivation of dhyāna that is not sequential? Answer: This can be sorted into four: first, clarifying what is sequential; second, clarifying what is not sequential; third, clarifying what is sequential-then-not-sequential; fourth, clarifying what is not-sequential-then-sequential.

What is sequential is as explained above — the Larger Sūtra says: "The bodhisattva practices in sequence, studies in sequence, and walks the path in sequence." What is not sequential: the bodhisattva who cultivates the Lotus samādhi, the samādhi of a single practice, and the like, contemplating the equal dharma-realm as neither deep nor shallow — this is called not sequential. As the Sūtra of Measureless Meanings says: "Walking the great, direct road, with nothing left to hinder it."

zh: 次第非次第者，如《大品》中須菩提白佛：「次第心應行般若，應生般若，應修般若不？」佛告須菩提：「常不離薩婆若故，為行般若，為生般若，為修般若。」非次第次第者，如須菩提白佛：「一切諸法皆無自性，云何菩薩得從一地至一地？」佛告須菩提：「以諸法空故，菩薩得從一地至一地。」
en: What is sequential-then-not-sequential: as in the Larger Sūtra, where Subhūti addresses the Buddha, saying: "Should one practice prajñā with a sequential mind, give rise to prajñā, and cultivate prajñā?" The Buddha tells Subhūti: "Because one is never apart from omniscience, one thereby practices prajñā, gives rise to prajñā, and cultivates prajñā."

What is not-sequential-then-sequential: as when Subhūti addresses the Buddha, saying: "If all dharmas whatsoever are without any nature of their own, how can a bodhisattva pass from one ground to the next?" The Buddha tells Subhūti: "Precisely because all dharmas are empty, the bodhisattva is able to pass from one ground to the next."

zh: 問曰：今此四句但據菩薩，亦得通二乘否？答曰：二乘亦得作此說。何以故？知自有聲聞初發心行於行行，從根本初禪而修，乃至超越禪，方得阿羅漢果，是為次第。或有聲聞人聞說善來，一時具足三明、八解脫等，是為非次第。或有聲聞人修次第行行時即用慧行，善觀次第性空，從初心，乃至得阿羅漢，是名次第非次第。四、或有聲聞從初發心即修慧行，發電光三昧，得四果，未具諸禪，為欲滿足有為功德故，次第修五種禪定滿足，即是非次第而次第也。此義至第七、釋修證及第八、顯示果報等十意竟，即自分明。
en: Question: These four statements have just been given in terms of the bodhisattva — do they also apply to the two lesser vehicles? Answer: The two lesser vehicles can also be spoken of in this same way. Why is this? It is known that there are śrāvakas who, from their very first arising of the mind, practice practice-conduct, cultivating from the root first dhyāna onward, all the way to the transcendence dhyāna, only then attaining the fruit of arhatship — this is what is sequential. There are also śrāvakas who, upon simply hearing the words "welcome, come forth," become complete all at once in the three insights, the eight liberations, and the rest — this is what is not sequential. There are also śrāvakas who, while cultivating practice-conduct in sequence, make use of wisdom-conduct at the same time, skillfully contemplating the emptiness of the nature of that very sequence, from the first mind onward, all the way to attaining arhatship — this is called sequential-then-not-sequential. Fourth, there are also śrāvakas who, from the very first arising of the mind, cultivate wisdom-conduct directly, give rise to the lightning-flash samādhi, and attain the four fruits without yet being complete in the full range of dhyānas — and then, wishing to fulfill conditioned merit completely, cultivate the five kinds of dhyāna-concentration in sequence to completion — this is precisely what is not-sequential-then-sequential. This point will become clear of itself once the seventh topic, explaining cultivation and realization, and the eighth, revealing the fruits and rewards, and the rest of the ten topics are complete.

This four-part grid — sequential, non-sequential, sequential-then-non-sequential, non-sequential-then-sequential — is a recognizably Tiantai move: rather than picking a side in "is the path gradual or sudden," Zhiyi sorts canonical proof-texts for both into a single fourfold scheme, and then, in the closing exchange, shows the same fourfold scheme applies just as well to the śrāvaka path as to the bodhisattva's. The overall effect undercuts any simple claim that "gradual" and "sudden" sort neatly by vehicle — both patterns of practice show up on both paths. This closes topic 4.

parent: V. Discriminating the Dharma and Mind of Dhyāna-Pāramitā

zh: 已略說諸禪詮次竟，諸禪中法心之相復應知之。今就明法心中，即為三意：一、先辨法；二、明心；三、分別簡定法心之別。就第一、先辨法中，法有四種：一、有漏法；二、無漏法；三、亦有漏亦無漏法；四、非有漏非無漏法。
en: Now that the sequence of the various dhyānas has been briefly explained, the mark of the dharma and the mind within these dhyānas should also be known. Here, in clarifying dharma and mind, there are three parts: first, distinguishing dharma; second, clarifying mind; third, discriminating and settling the distinction between dharma and mind.

First, distinguishing dharma: dharma is of four kinds — first, contaminated dharma; second, uncontaminated dharma; third, both contaminated and uncontaminated dharma; fourth, neither contaminated nor uncontaminated dharma.

zh: 一、有漏法者，謂十善、根本四禪、眾生緣四無量心、四空定是。所以者何？此十二門禪，體非觀慧之法，不能照了斷諸煩惱故。二、無漏法者，九想、八念、十想、背捨、勝處、一切處、次第定、師子奮迅、超越三昧、四諦十六行、十二因緣法緣四無量心、三十七品、三三昧，乃至願智、頂禪、十一智、三無漏根等諸無漏定是。所以者何？此諸禪中悉有對治，觀慧具足，能斷三漏故。三、亦有漏亦無漏法者，六妙門、十六特勝、通明等是。所以者何？此三種禪中雖有觀慧對治，力用劣弱，故名亦有漏亦無漏。四、非有漏非無漏法者，法華三昧、般舟念佛、首楞嚴等百八三昧，自性禪等九種禪，乃至無緣大慈大悲、十波羅蜜、四無礙智、十八空、十力、四無所畏、十八不共法、一切種智等是。所以者何？修是等法，不墮二邊，故名非有漏非無漏法。
en: First, contaminated dharma: this refers to the ten wholesome deeds, the root four dhyānas, the four immeasurable minds taken with sentient beings as their object, and the four formless concentrations. Why is this? These twelve gates of dhyāna are not, in their own nature, dharmas of contemplative wisdom, and so are unable to illuminate and sever the afflictions.

Second, uncontaminated dharma: this refers to the nine contemplations, the eight recollections, the ten contemplations, the liberations, the stations of mastery, the totality-bases, the sequential concentrations, the lion's-sport and transcendence samādhis, the sixteen aspects of the Four Noble Truths, the twelve links of dependent origination, the four immeasurable minds taken with dharmas as their object, the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment, the three samādhis, and on through wish-wisdom, the summit-dhyānas, the eleven kinds of knowledge, the three uncontaminated faculties, and the other uncontaminated concentrations. Why is this? Within all these dhyānas there is, in every case, an antidote at work, contemplative wisdom complete, able to sever the three contaminants.

Third, both contaminated and uncontaminated dharma: this refers to the six wondrous gates, the sixteen special excellences, the thorough-and-bright contemplation, and the like. Why is this? Although these three kinds of dhyāna do contain contemplative wisdom as an antidote, its power and function are weak, and so they are called both contaminated and uncontaminated.

Fourth, neither contaminated nor uncontaminated dharma: this refers to the Lotus samādhi, the buddha-recollection samādhi of pratyutpanna, the hundred and eight samādhis beginning with the Śūraṅgama, the nine dhyānas beginning with the dhyāna of self-nature, and on through unconditioned great loving-kindness and great compassion, the ten pāramitās, the four unhindered wisdoms, the eighteen emptinesses, the ten powers, the four kinds of fearlessness, the eighteen unshared qualities, the wisdom that knows all things in every mode, and the like. Why is this? Cultivating these dharmas does not fall into either extreme — hence they are called neither contaminated nor uncontaminated dharma.

This fourfold grid resorts everything named across topics 3 and 4 by a new criterion: not which gate it's entered through, or where it falls in sequence, but how completely it cuts through affliction. The twelve gates of dhyāna (topic 4's foundational attainments) turn out to be merely contaminated on their own — concentration without the wisdom to dismantle delusion. The bodhisattva's nine unshared dhyānas, by contrast, land in the most radical category of all: not just "uncontaminated" but "neither contaminated nor uncontaminated," a distinction the next passage goes on to explain.

quiz.q: Which order correctly gives the śrāvaka's sequence of uncontaminated wisdom-conduct?
options: the nine contemplations → eight recollections → ten contemplations
hearing the truths → the thirty-seven factors → the three gates of liberation → the sixteen aspects → the ten knowledges and three faculties, nine cultivations and nine severances
the gates of liberation → hearing the truths → the ten knowledges
the twelve links → the four truths → the thirty-seven factors
quiz.why: "Upon hearing the Four Noble Truths, one cultivates the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment; next enters the three gates of liberation; next uses the sixteen aspects of contemplation to distinguish the Four Noble Truths; next becomes complete in the ten kinds of knowledge and the three uncontaminated faculties." The twelve links belong to the pratyekabuddha, and the nine contemplations to practice-conduct.

quiz.q: When the bodhisattva accomplishes in sequence the knowledge and severance of the two vehicles' trainees and adepts, what is it called?
options: the non-sequential
entering the provisional from emptiness
entering emptiness by way of the provisional, complete with thorough contemplation
the contemplation of the middle way
quiz.why: "As for the bodhisattva accomplishing, in sequence, the knowledge and severance attained by both the trainees and the adepts of the two lesser vehicles — this is called 'entering emptiness by way of the provisional,' complete with thorough contemplation." The Larger Sūtra adds that the bodhisattva passes through these grounds "yet without taking hold of their realization."

quiz.q: Which set belongs entirely to the bodhisattva's nine unshared dhyānas?
options: every gate, nine sequential concentrations, removing affliction, thorough-and-bright
self-nature, lion's-sport, transcendence, difficult
self-nature, difficult, good person, pure-and-undefiled
every meaning, sixteen excellences, joy in this and later lives, eight liberations
quiz.why: The nine are self-nature, every meaning, difficult, every gate, the good person, every practice, removing affliction, joy in this life and lives to come, and pure-and-undefiled. The lion's-sport, transcendence, nine sequential concentrations, and eight liberations are shared with the two vehicles; the sixteen excellences and thorough-and-bright are both contaminated and uncontaminated.

quiz.q: When first learning dhyāna, must a practitioner follow the sequence above step by step?
options: beginners may not cultivate dhyāna
yes, no step may be skipped
beginners may only practice the non-sequential
no; a beginner follows what they are inclined to and what best serves as an antidote, without necessarily following each step
quiz.why: "What has just been said is meant only to clarify the shallow-to-deep pattern among the various dhyānas in a general way ... As for a beginning student, they should follow whatever they find most inclined toward and easiest to apply as an antidote." The sequence maps depth; it is not a rigid rule.

quiz.q: In the fourfold scheme, what example does the text give of "not sequential"?
options: the bodhisattva cultivating the Lotus samādhi, the single-practice samādhi, and the like, contemplating the equal dharma-realm as neither deep nor shallow
cultivating from the first root dhyāna to transcendence
passing from ground to ground because dharmas are empty
first the five dhyānas, then the four fruits
quiz.why: "What is not sequential: the bodhisattva who cultivates the Lotus samādhi, the samādhi of a single practice, and the like, contemplating the equal dharma-realm as neither deep nor shallow — this is called not sequential." Passing from ground to ground is not-sequential-then-sequential, and going from the first dhyāna up to transcendence is sequential.

quiz.q: For "not-sequential-then-sequential," Subhūti asks how a bodhisattva can pass from one ground to the next if all dharmas lack self-nature. How does the Buddha answer?
options: because dharmas do have self-nature
because one is never apart from omniscience
precisely because all dharmas are empty, the bodhisattva can pass from one ground to the next
the bodhisattva cannot pass between grounds
quiz.why: "The Buddha tells Subhūti: 'Precisely because all dharmas are empty, the bodhisattva is able to pass from one ground to the next.'" Emptiness is what makes sequence possible. "Never apart from omniscience" is the proof-text for sequential-then-not-sequential.

quiz.q: The fourfold scheme applies to the two vehicles too. Which case is the śrāvaka's "not sequential"?
options: first the lightning-flash samādhi and the four fruits, then the five dhyānas in sequence
using wisdom-conduct while cultivating practice-conduct, contemplating the emptiness of the sequence
cultivating from the first root dhyāna to transcendence before arhatship
upon hearing "welcome, come forth," becoming complete all at once in the three insights, eight liberations, and the rest
quiz.why: "There are also śrāvakas who, upon simply hearing the words 'welcome, come forth,' become complete all at once in the three insights, the eight liberations, and the rest — this is what is not sequential." The other three options are the sequential, sequential-then-not-sequential, and not-sequential-then-sequential cases.

quiz.q: Why are the ten wholesome deeds, the root four dhyānas, the immeasurables taking beings as object, and the formless concentrations "contaminated dharma"?
options: because they are evil
because their wisdom is complete but weak
these twelve gates are not in nature dharmas of contemplative wisdom, and cannot illuminate and sever afflictions
because only non-Buddhists practice them
quiz.why: "These twelve gates of dhyāna are not, in their own nature, dharmas of contemplative wisdom, and so are unable to illuminate and sever the afflictions." They are wholesome and practiced by Buddhists too; weak contemplative wisdom is the reason given for the "both" category.
